title: Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing of Copper Nickel and Nickel Aluminum Bronze: A Microscopy Driven Microstructure-Property Study
content: Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) presents a promising solution for producing high-quality parts with complex geometries while minimizing material waste. In this study, we explore the application of WAAM to fabricate components using copper-nickel (CuNi) through various AM systems to understand the relationship between systems and microstructure evolution, and nickel aluminum bronze (NAB) alloys to study the effect of cooling rate variation on microstructure evolution. We employed advanced microscopy techniques, including scanning electron microscopy (SEM), electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) to analyze the microstructural characteristics of these materials and their corresponding processes. This research demonstrates the feasibility and advantages of using WAAM for the fabrication of CuNi and NAB parts, emphasizing the critical role of microscopy in characterizing and optimizing material properties. The outcomes underscore WAAM's potential to improve efficiency and performance in the casting and forging sector [1].
